title: Site-directed mutagenesis
author: Johannes Stuttmann
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.behgjb3w
materials: Primer Design: here examplified by an amino acid exchange within a coding sequence Primer 1: AGTCTCCAACCAAGcTCCAATCCCAAGAT Primer 2: ATCTTGGGATTGGAgCTTGGTTGGAGACT • the mismatch = desired exchange should be in the middle of the oligo • there are rules / calculators for primer length and annealing temperature; for example https://depts.washington.edu/bakerpg/primertemp/ • but a rule of thumb normally also does the job: exchange of a single nt: design primers of 27 nt length exchange of 2-3 nt: design primers of 29-30 nt length exchange of more 4-7 nt: 15-18 nt on each side • for more extensive modifications, things may get complicated • primers may also be designed to produce insertions or deletions… but this may require more careful design Critical points: • Ratio template : primers. Let’s consider that a normal plasmid preparation has a concentration around 100 ng/µl, and plasmids are of 3 – 10 kb in size. A good starting point will be to use a 1:5 dilution of your plasmid in the PCR reaction (2 µl in 20 µl reaction), together with 1 µl of the primers @ 5 µM. • The polymerase. Not every polymerase works well for SDM, and one may work for one reaction, while the other one will perform better in the next reaction. I advise using a Pfu polymerase (e.g. PfuPlus! DNA Polymerase from Roboklon) and one of the “chimeric” DNA polymerases (Phusion Polymerase, Q5 (both NEB), Polymerase X (Roboklon) or similar) in parallel, as one will normally do the job on a given molecule.

steps.title: Prepare PCR Reaction Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the PCR reaction using either PfuPlus! or Hybrid (Polymerase X) DNA polymerase according to the following compositions:

substeps.instruction: For PfuPlus!: 2 µl PfuPlus! Polymerase, 1 µl Primer 1 (5 µM), 1 µl Primer 2 (5 µM), 2 µl dNTPs (2mM), 2 µl 10 x PCR buffer, 0.3 µl Pfu Polymerase, 5–50 ng template DNA, and 11.7 µl H2O (Total 20 µl).

For Hybrid Polymerase: 2 µl Hybrid Polymerase, 1 µl Primer 1 (5 µM), 1 µl Primer 2 (5 µM), 1 µl dNTPs (2mM), 2 µl 10 x PCR buffer, 0.3 µl Hybrid polymerase, 5–50 ng template DNA, and 12.7 µl H2O (Total 20 µl).

steps.title: Perform PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Run the PCR using the conditions corresponding to the chosen polymerase:

substeps.instruction: PfuPlus! conditions: 95 °C 1 min; then 18 cycles of (95 °C 30 sec, 56 °C 30 sec, 68 °C 1 min/kb); final extension 68 °C 6 min.
Hybrid Polymerase conditions: 98 °C 30 sec; then 18 cycles of (98 °C 10 sec, 58 °C 20 sec, 72 °C 30 sec/kb); final extension 72 °C 4 min.

steps.title: Verify PCR Results
steps.instruction: Verify the amplification by loading 5 µl of the PCR product onto a 1% agarose gel to check for a visible band.

steps.title: Perform DpnI Digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the template DNA by adding DpnI directly to the remaining PCR reaction.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.3 – 0.5 µl of DpnI to the PCR mix.
Incubate for 1 hour to overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Transform E. coli
steps.instruction: Transform the digested linear DNA into E. coli cells.

substeps.instruction: If using chemically competent cells, the entire reaction can be transformed.
Plate 10% of the transformation to obtain approximately 10 – 1000 clones.

steps.title: Isolate and Verify Mutagenized Plasmid
steps.instruction: Confirm the mutation through colony picking and sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Pick 2 single colonies and inoculate small liquid cultures.
Verify the sequence to ensure the desired mutation is present and check for primer integration or second-site mutations.
